فَعْمٌ Full; applied in this sense to a سَاعِد [or fore arm]; (S, K;) and to a vessel; as also ↓ فَعْمَلٌ , in which the ل is augmentative: (K:) and full of flesh; applied to the place of the anklet. (TA.) It is said of the Prophet, in a trad., كَانَ فَعْمَ الأَوْصَال i. e. He was full in respect of the limbs. (TA.) And one says اِمْرَأَةٌ فَعْمَةٌ A woman full-formed, and thick in her shank. (K.) And حَاضِرٌ فَعْمٌ A [great] tribe filled with its people. (TA.) [See also مُفْعَمٌ: and see أَفْعَمُ.] ＝
-A2- And A species of tree: or the rose. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
